correctness.rationale: Independently reconstructed complete three-state forest transfer, four marked-edge completion counts and three rational covariance factorizations; all coefficients imply strict negativity for n>=2. Exact verifier enumerated all subsets for n=2..6 and checked 8,059 assertions/comparisons including integer polynomial identities and 2..2000 finite parameters. Enumeration supplements an unrestricted combinatorial argument.

evidence: Semple–Welsh, UCDMS2005/12, Theorem 4.4 (report p.13): graphs obtained from K4-or-smaller 2-connected blocks by series/parallel additions.
Erickson, arXiv:1008.3660, Theorem 1.2 (p.2): series-parallel graphs satisfy a Rayleigh sum-of-squares identity.
Altar Çiçeksiz–Ravichandran, arXiv:2610.00549, introduction pp.2–4: broad all-graph inequality still conjectural; high-fugacity and complete-graph results have different hypotheses.
broader_coverage.reasoning: For n>=3, K_{3,n} contains K_{3,3} and is 3-vertex-connected with at least six vertices, so it cannot be a series/parallel extension of K4 blocks, which would have a 2-separation unless already a base block. Thus the cited family results do not imply the new infinite family. The general forest conjecture is not a theorem.

originality.rationale: Claim-level comparisons checked the original Grimmett–Winkler conjecture/small cases; Semple–Welsh K4-block extension theorem; Erickson series-parallel theorem; and 2026 general forest results. K_{3,n} for n>=3 lies beyond the cited graph-family hypotheses; no searched source states the three closed covariance formulas. Historical priority not independently certified.
residual_risks: An unlocated complete-bipartite forest-enumerator paper could implicitly provide some/all orbit formulas.
A broad matroid theorem with hypotheses not identified in the reviewed sources might imply unit-weight edge negative correlation, although the standard graph-class results inspected do not.
Search coverage does not constitute independent priority certification.

value.rationale: Settles three edge-pair orbits in an infinite 3-connected, non-series-parallel bipartite graph family of the classical forest negative-correlation conjecture. Exact formulas reveal constant local anticorrelation and distinct quadratic-decay nonlocal rates, extending beyond the earlier bounded numerical checks without claiming the general conjecture.
